definitions.gloss: see you later; see you again
definitions.explanation: A friendly, casual way to say goodbye with the implication of meeting again.

examples.japanese: またね！{楽|たの}しかったよ。
examples.english: See you later! It was fun.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}はありがとう。またね。
examples.english: Thanks for today. See you later.

examples.japanese: {電話|でんわ}を{切|き}る{前|まえ}に「またね」と{言|い}った。
examples.english: I said "see you" before hanging up the phone.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}で{友達|ともだち}と{別|わか}れるとき、「またね」と{手|て}を{振|ふ}った。
examples.english: When parting with my friend at the station, I waved and said "see you later."

notes:
またね comes from また (again) + ね (sentence-ending particle), literally meaning "again, okay?" It implies you expect to see the person again.

REGISTER:
Casual and friendly. Used among friends, family, and peers. Not appropriate in formal situations — use {失礼|しつれい}します or さようなら instead.

VARIATIONS:
- またね: standard casual goodbye
- また: even more casual (dropping ね)
- また{明日|あした}ね: see you tomorrow
- また{今度|こんど}ね: see you next time
- また{会|あ}おうね: let's meet again (slightly warmer)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- じゃあね: see you (casual, slightly more abrupt)
- バイバイ: bye-bye (casual, younger speakers)
- さようなら: goodbye (formal; can imply a longer separation)
- {失礼|しつれい}します: goodbye (polite/formal, workplace)
